description: SaaS Tool Expert Pack. Covers user accounts, tenant/workspace isolation, subscription plans, usage quotas, AI generation cost tracking, API/provider key safety, billing webhooks, admin console, and rate limiting. Does NOT constitute a complete multi-tenant production SaaS platform.

supported_surfaces.purpose: SaaS dashboard: user workspace, generation UI, subscription management
REST API: tenants, users, subscriptions, quotas, generations, webhooks, rate limiting
Persistent storage: tenants, users, subscriptions, quotas, generation history, API keys
Async generation processing, webhook handling, quota refresh, billing sync
Admin console: tenant management, plan management, usage monitoring, key management
API documentation, integration guide, rate limit policy, security policy

default_surface_templates.description: Full SaaS platform with admin, billing webhooks, rate limiting
AI SaaS platform with multiple providers, usage tracking, multi-tenancy

domain_risk_rules.reason: Tenant isolation errors cause cross-tenant data leaks
Subscription gating errors cause unauthorized access to paid features
Quota deduction bugs cause revenue loss or over-provisioning
API key exposure causes security breach and provider cost theft
Provider keys must never reach client-side code
Non-idempotent billing webhooks cause duplicate charges
Unrecorded generation costs cause billing discrepancies
Missing rate limits cause resource exhaustion and cost spikes
Permission escalation gives unauthorized admin access
Generated content ownership issues cause compliance violations

business_invariants.description: Every data access must be scoped to the current tenant_id. Cross-tenant access is forbidden.
business_invariants.violation_example: User from tenant A querying data from tenant B
business_invariants.valid_example: All queries filtered by WHERE tenant_id = current_tenant_id

business_invariants.description: Users belonging to one tenant cannot access data from another tenant
business_invariants.violation_example: Changing tenant_id query param to access another tenant's generations
business_invariants.valid_example: Tenant derived from authenticated user context, not request param

business_invariants.description: Feature access must be gated by current subscription status
business_invariants.violation_example: Expired subscription user generating AI content
business_invariants.valid_example: Middleware checks subscription_status before allowing generation

business_invariants.description: Users with expired or cancelled subscriptions cannot invoke generation endpoints
business_invariants.violation_example: Cancelled plan still allows AI generation requests
business_invariants.valid_example: Route guard returns 402 Payment Required for expired subscriptions

business_invariants.description: Usage quota remaining must never be negative
business_invariants.valid_example: Quota decrement checks remaining >= delta before allowing

business_invariants.description: Quota decrement must be atomic to prevent race conditions under concurrent requests
business_invariants.violation_example: Two concurrent requests both pass quota check, resulting in double-decrement
business_invariants.valid_example: Database-level atomic decrement with conditional UPDATE

business_invariants.description: Every AI generation must record its token cost for billing purposes
business_invariants.violation_example: AI generation succeeds but cost is not recorded in billing ledger
business_invariants.valid_example: After generation completes, cost entry is persisted with tenant_id, token_count, model, timestamp

business_invariants.description: All generation history entries must be scoped to and owned by the tenant
business_invariants.violation_example: Generation history endpoint returns results from other tenants
business_invariants.valid_example: Generation history query filtered by authenticated user's tenant_id

business_invariants.description: API keys and secrets must never appear in client-facing responses, logs, or error messages
business_invariants.violation_example: GET /api/keys returns full api_key value in response body
business_invariants.valid_example: API returns only key_id, masked_last_four, and created_at — never the full key

business_invariants.description: Provider API keys (OpenAI, Claude, etc.) must be stored and used only server-side; never in client bundles
business_invariants.violation_example: OPENAI_API_KEY included in frontend .env or config.js
business_invariants.valid_example: Provider key stored in server environment or vault, accessed only by backend services

business_invariants.description: Billing webhooks (Stripe, Paddle, etc.) must be processed idempotently — duplicate events must not double-process
business_invariants.violation_example: Receiving the same invoice.paid event twice creates two credits
business_invariants.valid_example: Webhook handler checks event_id deduplication table before processing

business_invariants.description: Rate limiting must be enforced — per user, per tenant, or per IP — and not bypassable
business_invariants.violation_example: Single user making 1000 generation requests per second without restriction
business_invariants.valid_example: Middleware returns 429 Too Many Requests after limit exceeded

business_invariants.description: Only admin roles can change subscription plans or quotas
business_invariants.violation_example: Regular user upgrading own plan without payment
business_invariants.valid_example: Plan change endpoint requires ADMIN role and audit log entry

business_invariants.description: Deleted or disabled workspaces cannot access any API endpoints
business_invariants.violation_example: Soft-deleted workspace still processing generation requests
business_invariants.valid_example: Workspace status check in auth middleware returns 403 for deleted workspaces

required_external_engines.note: Security static analysis — API key exposure, tenant isolation, injection, auth bypass
API load smoke for rate limit and generation endpoints
Structured load testing for rate limit verification

human_audit_points: Billing and subscription logic — must be reviewed by business owner
API key and provider key handling — must be reviewed by security reviewer
Tenant isolation design — must be reviewed by architecture reviewer
Quota and credit deduction logic — must be reviewed by business owner
Webhook idempotency — must be reviewed by security reviewer
Admin permission model — must be reviewed by security reviewer
Production-scale performance claims — require architecture review and load test evidence

non_claims: This pack does NOT constitute a complete, production-ready multi-tenant SaaS platform
This pack does NOT include actual payment gateway integration (Stripe/Paddle code)
This pack does NOT include SOC2/ISO27001 compliance certification
This pack does NOT include GDPR/data-privacy compliance implementation
This pack does NOT include real AI model provider integration (only design patterns)
This pack does NOT include production-scale multi-region deployment
This pack does NOT include SSO/SAML/OIDC enterprise auth integration
This pack is a DESIGN AID — domain rules, invariants, and test patterns
Actual implementation requires domain expert review, security audit, and production hardening
